verdict.rationale_short: The morning HOLD upgrade was premised on a CPI print below the 4.2% consensus; the actual BLS release confirmed 4.2% YoY headline — at the 3-year high consensus, not below it. The initial market bounce was a head-fake that fully reversed as Iran escalation intensified. SPX closed at 7,266.99 (−1.62%), below both the 7,460 regime floor and the morning brief's explicit 7,300 BEARISH trigger. Four of five regime indicators are now in breach (VIX, 30Y, DXY, SPX). Brent at $93.10 — $3.90 below the $97 trigger — is the remaining buffer; until that breaks, STEP ASIDE is the appropriate posture. Raise cash, hold short hedges, avoid new longs.

bear_case: The US-Iran exchange has moved beyond posturing into active mutual military strikes in the Strait of Hormuz region — making a negotiated resolution within days implausible. Gold's 4.44% sell-off on a geopolitical escalation day signals institutional forced deleveraging, not orderly rotation; this pattern historically precedes a second forced-selling wave 1-3 sessions later. SPX closed at 7,267, below the morning brief's explicit 7,300 BEARISH trigger, and the next support zone is 7,200-7,250. A hot May PPI Thursday (≥0.8% m/m) would push the 30Y through 5.0%, compress tech multiples further, and put Warsh in position to acknowledge July hike risk at the June 17 FOMC — a scenario currently priced at roughly 15% probability. Brent at $93.10 is $3.90 from the oil regime trigger; an active military exchange in Hormuz waters is not compatible with gradual oil normalization. Invalidation: if Brent settles back below $90 on confirmed Iran de-escalation and SPX reclaims 7,380 on two consecutive sessions, STEP ASIDE converts to HOLD.
